skill.name: architecture-diagram
skill.description: Creates dark-themed technical architecture diagrams as standalone HTML pages with inline SVG. Use it for system, cloud, security, infrastructure, and network topology diagrams.
skill.summary: Generate polished HTML and SVG architecture diagrams from technical system descriptions.
skill.author: Cocoon-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code, SVG examples, CSS colors, and diagram wording. The only confirmed issue is the Google Fonts dependency in SKILL.md and assets/template.html, which can trigger external network requests. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable command behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Generated diagrams may load Google Fonts from an external domain.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local font stack, embed the font, or clearly document the network request in the skill guidance and template.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear technical diagrams that show systems, networks, and cloud services. This skill guides AI tools to produce dark standalone HTML diagrams with inline SVG.
actual_capabilities: Defines a dark visual system for frontend, backend, database, cloud, security, and external components.
Provides reusable SVG patterns for component boxes, arrows, legends, security groups, and region boundaries.
Includes an HTML template with embedded CSS and inline SVG examples.
Explains spacing rules to avoid overlapping stacked components and message buses.
Guides headers, summary cards, footers, and metadata for finished diagram pages.
limitations: Generated output may load Google Fonts unless the external link is removed.
It does not infer architecture from live infrastructure or cloud accounts.
It provides guidance and a template, not an automated rendering engine.
Complex diagrams still require manual layout review for readability.

use_cases.title: Document a Product Architecture
use_cases.description: Create a clear diagram for services, databases, clients, and main data flows in a software product.

use_cases.title: Explain Cloud Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Show regions, security groups, load balancers, storage, and service boundaries for a cloud deployment.

use_cases.title: Review Security Flows
use_cases.description: Map authentication paths, protected resources, and network trust boundaries before a design review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic System Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small application diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture diagram for a web app with users, a frontend, an API service, and a PostgreSQL database.

prompt_templates.title: Diagram a Cloud Deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with cloud services and boundaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone HTML architecture diagram for an AWS deployment with CloudFront, S3, an application load balancer, API servers, and RDS.

prompt_templates.title: Show Security and Data Flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for security review preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security-focused architecture diagram that shows OAuth login, JWT validation, TLS paths, security groups, private services, and database access.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Complex Architecture Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for improving a crowded diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this architecture diagram plan to remove overlaps, place legends outside boundaries, group related services, and label every connection clearly.

output_examples.input: A SaaS app with browser users, React frontend, API service, Redis cache, PostgreSQL, and an auth provider.
output_examples.output: A dark HTML architecture page showing users, frontend, backend services, cache, database, auth flow, connection labels, and summary cards.

output_examples.input: An AWS static site with CloudFront, S3 buckets, API Gateway, Lambda functions, and DynamoDB.
output_examples.output: A cloud diagram with an AWS region boundary, service boxes, arrows for request paths, storage annotations, and deployment notes.

output_examples.input: A Kubernetes platform with ingress, services, workers, event bus, database, and external monitoring.
output_examples.output: A structured platform diagram with cluster boundaries, message bus placement, service groups, monitoring links, and an external legend.

best_practices: Provide the main components, boundaries, protocols, and data flows before asking for the diagram.
Review the SVG layout for overlaps after adding or removing services.
Keep legends outside region and cluster boundaries for cleaner diagrams.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a full diagram from vague product names without architecture details.
Do not place legends or summary text inside infrastructure boundaries.
Do not rely on the default template labels in a final deliverable.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates standalone HTML architecture diagrams with embedded CSS and inline SVG graphics.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate diagrams from live cloud accounts?
faq.answer: No. You must provide the architecture details that should appear in the diagram.

faq.question: Can the output work offline?
faq.answer: The HTML and SVG can work offline if the Google Fonts link is removed or replaced.

faq.question: What diagram styles are included?
faq.answer: It includes dark styling for cloud, frontend, backend, database, security, message bus, and external components.

faq.question: Is JavaScript required for the output?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for pure HTML, CSS animations, and inline SVG without JavaScript.
